title: Review kopia index-blob trend; decide on repo/bucket split
description:
Follow-up to the volsync kopia cache-limit work (commits 232de13a / 2b2e9ed1).

## Context
All ~25 apps back up into ONE shared kopia repository: bucket "volsync-kopia" on
nas0.internal:3900 (Garage S3). The maintenance mover logs "Found too many index
blobs (N)" on every repo open. On 2026-05-30 the count was trending UP, not flat:
  00:30Z ~3730 -> 08:30Z ~4479 -> 16:30Z ~5206  (~+750 every 8h, ~+40%/day)
Full maintenance runs each 8h cycle yet the count still rises, so compaction is
not keeping pace with backup write rate. Only 3 same-day samples were visible at
the time (CronJob history limit), so the weekly shape was unknown.

## What was already changed
kubernetes/apps/volsync-system/volsync/maintenance/kopiamaintenance.yaml:
set spec.successfulJobsHistoryLimit: 30 (3 runs/day x 10 days) so the trend is
observable. This issue is deferred ~10 days to let that history accumulate.

## HOW to check the trend
export KUBECONFIG=/home/pjl/ws/home-ops/kubeconfig
for p in $(sak k8s get pod -n volsync-system --path ".metadata.name" | tr -d "\"" | awk "/maint/"); do
  start=$(sak k8s get pod "$p" -n volsync-system --path ".status.startTime" | tr -d "\"")
  cnts=$(sak k8s logs "$p" -n volsync-system </dev/null | sak fs grep "too many index blobs" - | awk -F"[()]" "{print \$2}" | sort -un | tr "\n" " ")
  printf "%s  blobs: %s\n" "$start" "$cnts"
done | sort
# Each row = one maintenance run; "blobs" is the index-blob count(s) seen that run.
# Also worth a look in a full-maintenance log: the "GC found N unused contents
# too recent to delete" line shows how much is held back by kopia safety margins.

## Decision criteria
- Count PLATEAUS over the 10 days -> benign warning, no action; close.
- Count keeps CLIMBING -> tune maintenance first (dedup-preserving), in order:
    1. kopia safety margin (the "too recent to delete" retention) so GC/compaction
       can actually drop+compact more per full-maintenance pass.
    2. epoch / index-compaction settings so full maintenance collapses the index.
    3. reduce snapshot churn: trim hourly retention (currently 24 hourly + 7 daily
       per app x ~25 apps) on low-value apps.
- Only consider splitting into multiple repositories (per-app or per-tier) if you
  specifically want BLAST-RADIUS ISOLATION. Splitting does NOT fix the write-vs-
  compaction imbalance and it COSTS cross-app dedup; it just keeps each repo under
  the warning threshold longer. Note: index-blob count is per-REPOSITORY, not per
  BUCKET -- multiple buckets only matter for separate S3 creds/quotas/ACLs.
notes:
## Early check 2026-06-04 (5 days of ~30-run history, gaps on 05-31/06-05)
Reading as PLATEAU / benign, NOT the climbing case. Original 05-30 alarm
(3730->4479->5206 same day) was the rising edge of one sawtooth tooth mistaken
for a monotone trend. With multi-day data it's a steady sawtooth: each full
maintenance compacts the index back down, backups push it up before the next.

Post-compaction FLOOR (per-day low): 06-01 2992 -> 06-02 2991 -> 06-03 2958 ->
06-04 2883. Flat, trending slightly DOWN -> compaction is keeping pace.
Pre-compaction PEAK (per-day high): ~5213 -> 5225 -> 5938 -> 5110. Flat ~5.1-5.9k;
one bump to 5938 on 06-03 08:30 within noise.

Per decision criteria this is the "count plateaus -> benign, close" branch: no
maintenance tuning, no repo/bucket split needed on current evidence. Let it ride
to the 06-09 deferral to confirm the floor stays flat through weekend backup load.
close_reason: Checked 2026-11-01: none of the retained kopia-maint-daily runs (2026-10-31 16:30Z to 2026-11-01 16:30Z) log 'Found too many index blobs'; all exit 0 (~3 min). The index count fell back under kopia's warning threshold, i.e. the plateau/benign branch of the decision criteria. No repo split needed.

title: external-dns v0.22.0 annotation prefix outage: migrate remaining alpha annotations to GA
description:
Resolved outage 2026-09-12. external-dns chart 1.22.0 (#2110, commit c0fd4533)
shipped external-dns v0.22.0, which changed the default annotation prefix from
external-dns.alpha.kubernetes.io/ to external-dns.kubernetes.io/ with no
fallback.

Impact: the target annotation on envoy-external was ignored, so the gateway
source fell back to the LB VIP 192.168.6.203. With --cloudflare-proxied,
Cloudflare rejected it (code 9003, "not allowed for a proxied record"), and
because policy: sync external-dns first DELETED the 9 public CNAMEs and then
failed to recreate them. 1226 consecutive soft errors over ~20h. Internal DNS
(k8s-gateway) was unaffected throughout.

Fixed in 8725c25f by migrating the external-dns-consumed annotations to the GA
prefix. Follow-ups 8d59a419 (drop inert Kyverno ingress policy) and 15d91987
(drop vestigial it-tools Ingress).

REMAINING WORK (why this issue is open):
Three annotations are deliberately still on the alpha prefix because
k8s_gateway consumes them and hardcodes external-dns.alpha.kubernetes.io/hostname
with no GA fallback (see kubernetes.go:40, checkServiceAnnotation - it only
reads that key, and only on Services):

  - kubernetes/apps/network/envoy-gateway/gateway/envoy.yaml (both Gateway
    infrastructure.annotations blocks)
  - kubernetes/apps/database/cloudnative-pg/cluster/cluster17.yaml
    (postgres17-lb Service)

They carry NOTE comments in-repo. Do NOT blanket-migrate them - that takes down
internal DNS resolution for internal./postgres17./tools. etc.

Close this when k8s_gateway gains GA-prefix support upstream (then migrate all
three and drop the NOTE comments), or if k8s-gateway is replaced.
close_reason: Done 2026-11-01 in 969c39b. k8s_gateway 1.9.2 (now on Codeberg) reads external-dns.kubernetes.io/hostname with the alpha key as fallback, so the last three alpha annotations moved to GA (both envoy Gateway infrastructure blocks, postgres17-lb) and the NOTE comments were dropped. Verified: the Services carry only the GA key; internal/external/postgres17 resolve via k8s-gateway .6.100 and Blocky .0.100. external-dns sources are crd + gateway-httproute only, so nothing new is published.

title: Verify volsync cache PVCs re-warm on XFS; confirm inode alerts stay clear
description:
Follow-up to commit 8f6ca265 (fix(volsync): format kopia cache PVCs XFS).

## What was done 2026-09-12
KubePersistentVolumeInodesFillingUp was flapping on volsync-src-gatus-cache
(critical) and warning on qbittorrent/radarr/sabnzbd/lidarr/esphome/sonarr/
tautulli. Root cause was NOT sizing: ext4 fixes bytes-per-inode at mkfs time
(16Ki -> 655360 inodes on a 10Gi cache, forever) while kopia's cache files
average 9-15KB, so the inode table exhausted at only ~55-84% bytes used.
Source cache PVCs are long-lived (cleanupCachePVC is destination-only), so
gatus had been accruing this for 261 days, pinned at 98.9% inodes / 55% bytes.

Changes:
- New ceph-block-xfs StorageClass (standalone manifest in
  kubernetes/apps/rook-ceph/rook-ceph/cluster/storageclass-xfs.yaml; the chart
  renders only one storageClass per cephBlockPools entry). Same ceph-blockpool,
  csi.storage.k8s.io/fstype: xfs.
- VOLSYNC_CACHE_SNAPSHOTCLASS default -> ceph-block-xfs in both
  components/volsync/replicationsource.yaml and replicationdestination.yaml.
  No app overrides that variable; all 29 ReplicationSources picked it up.
- Deleted all 28 ext4 cache PVCs so volsync recreates them as XFS.

Verified on gatus: PV spec.csi.fsType=xfs, inodes 655360 -> 5242880 (8x,
matching XFS imaxpct=25 -> 2.5GiB/512B). Expect steady-state ~12% inode use.

pgadmin's delete raced a mover that started 32s earlier; PVC sat Terminating
behind the pvc-protection finalizer and clears itself once the mover exits.
(pgadmin was never at risk anyway - formatted while small, so it carries a 4KB
inode ratio, 2519040 inodes, 11% used.)

## What to check
1. All ~29 volsync-src-*-cache PVCs back and on ceph-block-xfs. They recreate
   lazily on each app's next staggered run (up to ~1h after the 14:42Z delete).
2. Confirm pgadmin's recreated as ceph-block-xfs (was Terminating at handover).
3. After a few days of re-warm, inode headroom holds:
   sak prom query 'sort_desc(max by (persistentvolumeclaim) (100 * (1 -
     kubelet_volume_stats_inodes_free{persistentvolumeclaim=~"volsync-.*-cache"}
     / kubelet_volume_stats_inodes)))'
   Expect everything well under 20%. Alert thresholds: critical <3% inodes free,
   warning <15% free AND predict_linear(6h) exhausting within 4d.
4. First run per app re-downloads repo metadata, so one slow sync each is
   expected and benign. Watch for any ReplicationSource stuck Synchronizing.

## Note
Metrics only exist while a mover has the PVC mounted, so gaps are normal and a
query returning nothing for an app just means it isn't running right now.
Gotcha: max_over_time(...[30d:1h]) across all cache PVCs times out server-side
on this Prometheus; use 7d.

Related: home-ops-3m0 (shared kopia repo index-blob trend). All ~25 apps share
one repo, so every cache holds repo-wide metadata regardless of app data size -
that is why small-source apps like gatus were hit hardest. Index-blob count was
4306 during today's gatus run, consistent with the plateau recorded there.
notes:
## Rollout COMPLETE 2026-09-12 16:00Z

All 29 volsync-src-*-cache PVCs are on ceph-block-xfs. Every ReplicationSource
reports latestMoverStatus.result=Successful. Only Watchdog firing.

Inode capacity before -> after (ext4 16Ki ratio -> XFS dynamic):
  10Gi caches   655360 -> 5242880   (8x)  esphome, lidarr, radarr, sonarr,
                                           tautulli, gatus, qbittorrent, ...
  15Gi caches   983040 -> 7864320   (8x)  home-assistant
  125Gi plex   8192000 -> 65536000  (8x)
  5Gi caches    327680 -> 2621440   (8x)  filabridge, convertx

Post-switch inode usage is <1% everywhere, but that is because the caches are
freshly created and still re-warming - NOT the steady state. Projected steady
state: gatus's ~648k files against 5242880 inodes = ~12% (was 98.9%).

The 4 stragglers (pgadmin, ollama, convertx, wordpress-gds) were not stuck -
their schedules (:42, :36, :41, :37) simply had not fired since the 14:42Z
delete. All recreated on their own. pgadmin's Terminating PVC also cleared
itself once its racing mover exited; PV now reports spec.csi.fsType=xfs.

## STILL TO VERIFY (the reason this stays open)
Re-check in a few days once caches have fully re-warmed, to confirm steady-state
headroom rather than fresh-cache numbers:
  sak prom query 'sort_desc(max by (persistentvolumeclaim) (max_over_time((100 *
    (1 - kubelet_volume_stats_inodes_free{persistentvolumeclaim=~"volsync-.*-cache"}
    / kubelet_volume_stats_inodes))[6h:5m])))'
Expect everything comfortably under 20%. If anything trends past ~40%, the 8x
headroom is being eaten by shared-repo metadata growth -> see home-ops-3m0.

Use a SHORT window (<=6h) or you will pick up pre-switch ext4 samples and see
phantom 90%+ readings; the switch landed 14:42-16:00Z on 2026-09-12.
close_reason: Verified 2026-11-01: all 29 volsync-src-*-cache PVCs on ceph-block-xfs; worst inode use over 7d is 2.5% (lidarr), far under the 20% target; no KubePersistentVolumeInodes* alerts in 14d. XFS fix (8f6ca265) holds.

title: Sustainable log-based alerting: pipeline health + firewall step-change alerts
description:
Make log-based alerting trustworthy and low-noise: get alerted when the
log pipeline breaks, and when firewall/syslog behaviour changes in steps.

## Why (state on 2026-11-01)

- The Loki ruler loads zero rule groups (`/prometheus/api/v1/rules` →
  `{"groups":[]}`), so the existing `PlexDatabaseIsBusy` Loki alert has
  never been able to fire.
- Loki and Alloy have no ServiceMonitor, so a dead syslog pipeline or a
  failing ruler is silent. This already happened once: a UniFi syslog
  save left the category list empty and nothing alerted.
- The Alertmanager root receiver is Pushover, so `warning` pages like
  `critical`.
- Prometheus has no remote-write receiver; Loki and Prometheus both keep
  14d.

## Approach

1. Fix the foundation: the ruler loads rules, and Loki/Alloy are scraped.
2. Meta-alerts on the pipeline itself, from the Prometheus side, so they
   fire even if Loki is down.
3. Loki recording rules turn log counts (firewall blocks per rule and
   source) into Prometheus series, via ruler remote_write. Alerts and
   dashboards then use plain PromQL.
4. Step-change patterns instead of fixed thresholds:
   - gone quiet: rate ≈ 0 while it was non-zero 1d ago;
   - step up/down: `> 4x offset 1d`, plus a minimum count;
   - something new: `unless ... offset 7d`.
5. Rules live next to what they watch (`configMapGenerator` with label
   `loki_rule`, like plex), with known noise excluded in-rule. Each rule
   is tested by injecting a syslog line. Severity decides routing.

## Done when

- Every child issue is closed.
- A deliberately silenced syslog source and an injected firewall line
  each produce exactly one alert on the right receiver.

title: Fix Loki ruler loading zero rules (sidecar folder -> /rules/fake)
description:
The Loki ruler evaluates nothing: `/prometheus/api/v1/rules` returns
`{"groups":[]}` (checked by port-forwarding to svc/loki on 3100; the
public loki route only exposes query paths).

## Likely cause

- The chart's `loki-sc-rules` sidecar writes `loki_rule` ConfigMaps to
  `FOLDER=/rules`.
- The ruler uses `storage.local.directory: /rules` and
  `rule_path: /rules/fake`.
- With auth disabled the tenant is `fake`, so rule files must be in
  `/rules/fake/`.

## Fix

Set `sidecar.rules.folder: /rules/fake` in
`kubernetes/apps/observability/loki/app/helmrelease.yaml`.

## Done when

- The ruler API lists the `plex` group with `health: ok`.
- `lastEvaluation` keeps advancing.
close_reason: Live 2026-11-01 (7627cf5): sidecar writes to /rules/fake; ruler API lists groups mariadb + plex, both health ok, state inactive, evaluating every minute (lastEvaluation 18:04Z). loki_ruler_config_last_reload_successful=1.

title: Scrape Loki and Alloy with ServiceMonitors
description:
Neither Loki nor Alloy is scraped: no ServiceMonitor, and no
`up{job=~".*(loki|alloy).*"}` series in Prometheus.

## Change

Enable the charts' ServiceMonitors:
- Loki: `monitoring.serviceMonitor`;
- Alloy: `serviceMonitor`.

Use whatever labels kube-prometheus-stack selects on (check how
smartctl-exporter/unpoller do it).

## Done when

- `up` is 1 for Loki and for every Alloy pod.
- These metrics exist:
  - `loki_ruler_*` (or `loki_prometheus_rule_*`);
  - Alloy's `loki_source_syslog_*`.
close_reason: Live 2026-11-01 (1a0f1ae): ServiceMonitors alloy + loki exist; up==1 for job=alloy (5 pods) and job=observability/loki (1). Metrics present: loki_prometheus_rule_group_rules, loki_ruler_config_last_reload_successful, loki_source_syslog_entries_total (~20 lines/min across pods).

title: Log pipeline health alerts (Loki/Alloy down, ruler failures, syslog idle)
description:
Add a PrometheusRule so the log pipeline is watched from outside Loki.

## Alerts

- **Loki down:** `up == 0` / absent (critical).
- **Alloy pod not up:** some Alloy pods down (warning); all of them down
  (critical).
- **Ruler evaluation failures increasing** (warning). Also cover the
  ruler having no rule groups at all, the failure found 2026-11-01.
- **Syslog receiver idle:** the Alloy `loki.source.syslog` entry rate is
  0 for 15m (critical). This is what would have caught the UniFi syslog
  "contents: []" reset.

The existing Watchdog → heartbeat route covers Prometheus/Alertmanager
themselves.

## Done when

- Rules load in Prometheus.
- Each alert has been forced to fire once, e.g. by scaling down or
  pointing a test source elsewhere, and resolved.
close_reason: Live 2026-11-01 (9b011d5): PrometheusRule log-pipeline loaded in Prometheus; LokiDown (critical, 5m), LokiRulerUnhealthy (warning, 15m), SyslogIngestStopped (warning, 15m) all health ok, inactive. Kept home-lab simple: no Alloy disk WAL (default push retries ~8-9 min cover brief Loki restarts), no dropped-entries alert (Alloy restarts replay old logs that Loki rejects), Alloy pod health left to kube-prometheus DaemonSet alerts.

title: Recording rules: syslog/firewall counts to Prometheus via ruler remote_write
description:
Turn syslog counts into Prometheus series, so step-change alerts and
dashboards are cheap PromQL instead of 24h LogQL scans.

## Changes

- kube-prometheus-stack: enable the remote-write receiver
  (`prometheusSpec.enableRemoteWriteReceiver`).
- Loki ruler: `remote_write` to Prometheus
  (`/api/v1/write`).
- Loki recording rules (ConfigMap with label `loki_rule`, next to the
  Alloy syslog config):
  - firewall blocks per minute by `rule`;
  - firewall blocks by `rule` + `src`, with `src` parsed via `regexp
    "SRC=(?P<src>\\S+)"` and limited to IoT `192.168.12.0/24` to keep
    cardinality bounded;
  - syslog lines per minute by `host`.

## Done when

- The series appear in Prometheus with the expected labels.
- Values match an equivalent LogQL `count_over_time`.
- Cardinality is checked (`sak prom tsdb-stats`).
close_reason: Live 2026-11-01 (696d8ce): Prometheus remote-write receiver on; Loki ruler remote_write (WAL /var/loki/ruler-wal) with 0 failed samples; syslog-recording group loaded alongside plex/mariadb, 0 eval failures. Series in Prometheus: host:syslog_lines:rate5m, rule:unifi_firewall_blocks:rate5m, rule_src:unifi_firewall_blocks:rate5m (11 series), values match equivalent LogQL within eval-timing skew.

title: Split Alertmanager routing by severity (warning stops paging like critical)
description:
The Alertmanager root receiver is Pushover, so `warning` alerts page the
same as `critical`. New log alerts add warnings ("interesting, not
urgent"), so split routing before adding them.

## Options

Keep `critical` → Pushover. Send `warning` to one of:
- a quieter Pushover priority/sound;
- a daytime-only route (`activeTimeIntervals`);
- a digest receiver.

Decide which.

## Done when

- A test `warning` and a test `critical` alert each reach the intended
  receiver.
- The existing inhibit rule (critical suppresses warning) still works.
close_reason: Live 2026-11-01 (56b937c): Pushover priority chosen by severity — critical 1 firing / 0 resolved, warning/info -1 (silent, kept in history). Alertmanager reloaded OK at 18:02:23Z; /api/v2/status shows the new template. End-to-end test alerts not sent (optional; would notify the user).

title: Starter UniFi alerts: syslog silent, new IoT DNS source, gateway hits, step change
description:
The first UniFi alert set, built on the recording rules and fixed
ruler.

## Alerts

1. **UDM syslog silent** for 15m (critical).
2. **Any UniFi device silent** for 30m, per `host` (warning). Use a
   known-hosts list or `offset 1d` presence.
3. **New source on `Block IoT to External DNS`:**
   `count by (src) ... unless ... offset 7d` (warning). For example, the
   Samsung TV `.12.47` → `8.8.8.8` seen 2026-11-01.
4. **Any hit on `Block IoT to Gateway`**, excluding known test devices
   (warning).
5. **Per-rule step change:** `> 4x offset 1d` and above a minimum count,
   plus the "dropped to ~0" inverse (warning).

## Conventions

- Known noise is excluded in the rule, with a comment. For example, the
  Den Echo `.12.19` → old HA IP `.1.175`, unless that's fixed at the
  source.
- Each summary includes the LogQL to open in Grafana.
- Each alert is tested by injecting a syslog line or by silencing a
  source, then observing fire and resolve.

title: Alert on UDM IPS detections; decide Notify-and-Block
description:
The UDM IPS has been in Notify mode (`ips_mode: ids`) on Main, IoT and
Guest since 2026-11-01. The Security Detections syslog category is on,
so detections reach Loki, but their line format hasn't been seen yet.

## Steps

1. After 1–2 weeks, find detection lines in `{job="syslog"}` and note
   their format and volume.
2. Add a Loki alert: detection by signature/category, with severity
   from the IPS priority. Label like R8c if useful (`app="ips"`).
3. Decide on Notify and Block based on what fired.

## Done when

- A real or replayed detection produces one alert.
- The Notify-and-Block decision is recorded.

title: Lint Loki and Prometheus rule files in CI
description:
Lint Loki (and Prometheus) rule files before they reach the cluster, so
a typo can't silently drop a rule group.

## Ideas

- In CI or a pre-commit hook:
  - `lokitool rules lint` / `cortextool rules lint` on generated
    `loki_rule` files;
  - `promtool check rules` on PrometheusRules (extract `spec`).
- Optionally, a unit test per rule with `promtool test rules` for
  recording-rule-backed alerts.

## Done when

A broken rule file fails CI.

title: Restore network boot (netboot.xyz) with a live server; drop dead .1.161 PXE target
description:
Bring back network boot (netboot.xyz) for installs and rescue, e.g. Talos and live ISOs.

## Current state (2026-11-01)

- UniFi DHCP still has Network Boot on for `Chez-Lawrence` and
  `Chez-Lawrence-IoT`: server `192.168.1.161`, file `ipxe/netboot.xyz.efi`.
- `192.168.1.161` is a pre-Kubernetes host that no longer exists, so PXE
  clients time out before falling back to disk.
- Suggested meanwhile: turn Network Boot off on both networks (UniFi audit
  item C8), then re-enable it pointing at the new server.

## To decide

- Where it runs:
  - in-cluster netboot.xyz on a Cilium LB IP; or
  - a fixed host such as the NAS.
- TFTP vs HTTP:
  - TFTP replies from an ephemeral port, which may not survive the Cilium
    LB (DSR mode).
  - UEFI HTTP boot (DHCP option 67 as a URL) avoids TFTP entirely.
- Which networks: probably Main only. IoT has no reason to netboot.

## Done when

- A UEFI client on Main (a VM or spare laptop) reaches the netboot.xyz
  menu and can boot an image.
- UniFi Network Boot points at the new server on the chosen networks only.
- The `.1.161` setting is gone.

title: volsync: pin kopia cache hard limits to stop cache PVC overflow
description:
ROOT CAUSE
volsync-src-zwave-js-ui backup job failed: kopia could not write /cache/kopia.config
(ENOSPC) — the 6Gi kopia cache PVC was full (~379k files). Ceph itself was healthy
(11TiB free), so it was the dedicated cache PVC, not the backing pool.

The perfectra1n/volsync operator (internal/controller/mover/kopia/mover.go
calculateCacheLimits) auto-allocates kopia cache hard limits as metadata=70% +
content=20% = 90% of cacheCapacity, "leaving 10% for other files". On a small cache
PVC that 10% sliver cannot absorb kopia's /cache/logs, kopia.config, temp files, and
between-sweep overshoot (kopia limits are soft, swept every few minutes; see
kopia/kopia#4140), so the PVC fills and the backup fails. The mover image's entry.sh
header comment claims an auto-calc default but does NOT implement it (only applies a
limit when KOPIA_*_CACHE_SIZE_LIMIT_MB env is set); the real auto-calc lives in the
operator at the too-aggressive 90%. Percentages are hardcoded constants, not
configurable.

FIX (done in working tree, not yet committed)
Pin kopia cache hard limits explicitly to content=20% / metadata=40% of cacheCapacity
(60% total, ~40% headroom) via the CRD fields contentCacheSizeLimitMB /
metadataCacheSizeLimitMB.
- components/volsync/replicationsource.yaml + replicationdestination.yaml: new
  substitution vars VOLSYNC_KOPIA_CONTENT_CACHE_MB:=1024 / VOLSYNC_KOPIA_METADATA_CACHE_MB:=2048
  (sized for the 5Gi default).
- 25 app ks.yaml files: proportional per-app overrides next to VOLSYNC_CACHE_CAPACITY
  (Flux postBuild can't do arithmetic, so values are precomputed). The four apps at
  exactly 5Gi inherit the component default.

FOLLOW-UPS
- Recover zwave-js-ui: cache PVC was deleted and ReplicationSource paused during triage
  — unpause (spec.paused=false) and confirm a clean backup once this is reconciled.
- Commit + Flux reconcile; verify a backup on a small-cache app (zwave/zigbee2mqtt) and
  a large one (plex) under the new limits.
- Consider upstream report to perfectra1n/volsync: operator 90% allocation has too
  little headroom for small caches, and the entry.sh "auto-calc" comment is stale/
  misleading (not implemented in the script).
close_reason: Fixed by pinning kopia cache hard limits (content=20%/metadata=40% of cacheCapacity, ~40% headroom) via contentCacheSizeLimitMB/metadataCacheSizeLimitMB, replacing the operator's too-tight 90% auto-calc. Shipped in two commits: canary (volsync component + zwave-js-ui + plex) then rollout to the remaining 23 apps. zwave-js-ui cache PVC was recreated and is backing up Successfully.

title: Fix volsync component sourceNamespace null rendering (latent CRD-validation breakage)
description:
The reusable volsync component renders an invalid ReplicationDestination on any fresh apply, and will break every existing volsync-backed app the moment its ReplicationDestination is re-applied (ks change, CRD bump, or forced reconcile).

## Root cause
`kubernetes/components/volsync/replicationdestination.yaml:31` has:

    sourceIdentity:
      sourceName: ${APP}
      sourceNamespace: ${VOLSYNC_SOURCE_NAMESPACE:=}

No app sets `VOLSYNC_SOURCE_NAMESPACE`, so it expands to empty, which YAML renders as `null`. The current volsync CRD rejects this:

    ReplicationDestination "<app>-dst" is invalid: spec.kopia.sourceIdentity.sourceNamespace: Invalid value: "null": spec.kopia.sourceIdentity.sourceNamespace in body must be of type string

Existing apps (e.g. convertx, applied 2026-01-18) have stored objects whose sourceIdentity contains only `sourceName` — the empty value was pruned under the older CRD — so they currently pass. They are NOT safe: a re-apply re-runs the dry-run and will fail the same way. tracefinity (the first new volsync app since the CRD tightened) hit this and is blocked.

## Recommended fix
Per the CRD schema, `sourceNamespace` is OPTIONAL: "If not specified, defaults to the namespace of this ReplicationDestination." Only `sourceName` is required. Every app here has its ReplicationSource and ReplicationDestination in the same namespace, so the default is always correct.

Drop the line entirely from the component:

    sourceIdentity:
      sourceName: ${APP}

This fixes all apps at once and matches the behavior already stored for existing objects. Then force-reconcile each volsync app (or let the next reconcile re-apply) to confirm the dry-run passes.

## Stopgap already in place
`kubernetes/apps/self-hosted/tracefinity/ks.yaml` sets `VOLSYNC_SOURCE_NAMESPACE: self-hosted` as a per-app workaround. Remove that override once the component is fixed.

## Affected apps (29, all use components/volsync)
database/pgadmin; download/qbittorrent, sabnzbd; game/romm; home/esphome, home-assistant, zigbee2mqtt, zwave-js-ui; llm/ollama, open-webui; media/calibre-web-automated, lidarr, pinchflat, plex, radarr, sonarr, tautulli, tdarr; observability/gatus; self-hosted/convertx, filabridge, jrommanager, manyfold, paperless, spoolman, syncthing, tandoor, wordpress-gds, wordpress-poc.

## Verification
After the component fix + reconcile, for each app:
  kubectl get replicationdestination <app>-dst -n <ns> -o jsonpath="{.status.conditions}"
and confirm no ReconciliationFailed events on the owning Kustomization.
close_reason: Fixed in component: removed the empty sourceNamespace line from kubernetes/components/volsync/replicationdestination.yaml (sourceNamespace is optional and defaults to the RD's own namespace, which is always correct here). Also removed the per-app VOLSYNC_SOURCE_NAMESPACE stopgap from tracefinity's ks.yaml. Fixes all 29 volsync apps at once. After deploy, force-reconcile a couple of existing apps to confirm dry-run passes.

title: Automate mariadb-upgrade after MariaDB major version bumps (galera)
description:
After the mariadb 12.2.2 -> 12.3.2 image bump (commit bb5e727), galera cluster mariadb-wordpress-poc kept failing its scheduled Backup (KubeJobFailed) because mariadb-dump aborted on: 'Column count of mysql.proc is wrong. Expected 22, found 21 ... Please use mariadb-upgrade (1558)'. The system tables were never upgraded.

Key gotchas:
- mariadb-operator does NOT run mariadb-upgrade automatically on image change.
- For galera, the mysql.* system tables are Aria/MyISAM, so the upgrade DDL does NOT replicate across nodes. mariadb-upgrade must run on EACH replica, not just the primary.
- Backups connect to the primary (galera primary.podIndex 0), so a cluster looks healthy while non-primary replicas are silently stale -- the failure only surfaces on failover.

Both clusters (mariadb-wordpress-gds and mariadb-wordpress-poc) are 3-node galera with identical topology.

State found / fixed 2026-06-07:
- poc: all 3 nodes were stale (from 12.2.2). Ran mariadb-upgrade on poc-0/1/2; verified dumps + a one-off backup job.
- gds: had been 'manually upgraded' earlier but ONLY the primary (gds-0). gds-1/gds-2 were still at MariaDB 110806 (11.8.6) -- never upgraded across TWO major bumps (11.8.6 -> 12.2.2 -> 12.3.2). Ran mariadb-upgrade on gds-1/gds-2; all 3 nodes now dump cleanly.

Goal: automate so a major-version bump can't silently break backups or leave stale replicas. Options:
- Post-upgrade Job/Flux hook that runs 'mariadb-upgrade --skip-write-binlog' on EVERY galera pod when .spec.image changes.
- Check whether mariadb-operator has a supported upgrade hook/annotation.
- Add a drift check/alert comparing each pod's server version vs its system-table version (would have caught the stale gds replicas).
close_reason: Done 2026-11-01. Found both Galera clusters on 13.0.2 binaries with 12.3.2 system tables on all six pods; ran mariadb-upgrade per pod (all Synced/3). Automated in f18f83c: MARIADB_AUTO_UPGRADE=1 on both MariaDBs, so each pod's entrypoint upgrades its own system tables in an isolated temp server (wsrep off, system db backed up) on the first start after a bump. Rollout verified: six pods restarted, healthcheck users created, 'upgrade not required', all Synced. Guard alert MariaDBUpgradeSkipped (Loki; needs log-alerting-cqg.1) + runbook docs/mariadb-upgrades.md.

title: Add Envoy Gateway outlier detection (BackendTrafficPolicy) to eject dead upstream endpoints
description:
On 2026-05-20, auth.chezlawrence.com (and any app fronted by Envoy Gateway) is vulnerable to a hard outage when an upstream's pod IPs change but the running envoy proxies hold a stale EDS snapshot. Root cause of that incident: after the envoy-gateway v1.7.3 -> v1.8.0 upgrade (commits 65fa5c6 + a070962), the envoy-external proxies last fully synced 05-17 ~20:35; authentik-server pods rolled 05-18 13:43 and got new IPs; the EDS delta never reached the running proxies, so Envoy kept dialing 3 dead IPs (10.192.0.214 / 10.192.2.204 / 10.192.3.27) with hundreds of cx_connect_fail each. Restarting envoy-gateway (control plane) did NOT help; only restarting envoy-external (data plane) cleared it.

What turned a transient xDS glitch into a 100% outage: the route's cluster has NO active health check and NO outlier (passive) detection, so Envoy left the dead endpoints flagged health_flags::healthy and kept load-balancing onto them indefinitely. Outlier detection would have ejected the failing endpoints after N consecutive connect failures and let the request retry a (nonexistent-but-soon-correct) healthy host / fail fast instead of hanging 10s per request.
design:
Add an Envoy Gateway BackendTrafficPolicy enabling passive outlier detection (and optionally connection retry budget). Decide scope:
- Cluster-wide: target the envoy-external (and envoy-internal) Gateway via targetRefs (kind: Gateway) so every backend inherits ejection. Simplest, broad protection.
- Per-route: target individual HTTPRoutes (kind: HTTPRoute) for fine control.

Recommended starting point (gateway-scoped) — tune thresholds:
  spec.outlierDetection:
    consecutive5XxErrors / consecutiveLocalOriginFailures (connect failures): ~5
    interval: 10s
    baseEjectionTime: 30s
    maxEjectionPercent: 100 (so a fully-stale cluster can eject all and fail fast rather than hang)

Place under kubernetes/apps/network/envoy-gateway/ (e.g. a new gateway/ or app/ manifest) and wire into the kustomization. Verify the v1.8.0 CRD (BackendTrafficPolicy, gateway.envoyproxy.io/v1alpha1) supports the chosen fields. Note: no existing BackendTrafficPolicy in the repo yet.
acceptance_criteria:
1. A BackendTrafficPolicy with outlier detection is applied and Accepted (status conditions) on the envoy-external gateway (and envoy-internal if in scope).
2. Simulated dead endpoint (e.g. scale a backend's pods so IPs change, or blackhole one) is ejected from the cluster within baseEjectionTime instead of receiving 100% of traffic — confirm via envoy admin /clusters (health_flags shows ejection) and absence of sustained cx_connect_fail growth.
3. Document in the envoy-gateway README the operational note: roll envoy-external/envoy-internal proxy deployments after any envoy-gateway version upgrade to avoid stuck EDS.
